title: Operator cutover chronicle and customer communication template — VPC private deployments
author: Maya Chen
content:
Summary:
This document is a single-source runbook and communications bundle for operator-led cutovers, blue/green switchover events, and controlled tenant migrations in VPC/private deployments. It is intended for field operators, SREs, and the customer success team. The artifact includes a step-by-step chronicle for operators, explicit evidence collection templates required for regulated customers, and prewritten customer communications for each cutover phase.

Scope and intent:
- Scope: VPC-hosted private deployments (single-tenant and multi-tenant topologies) undergoing planned cutovers, model swaps, KV-cache migrations, and control-plane handoffs.
- Intent: ensure predictable operator behavior, consistent evidence for compliance reviewers, and clear customer-facing messaging during each stage of a cutover.

Audience:
- Operators (field engineers) executing the cutover
- SRE/oncall verifying SLOs and monitoring
- Customer Success & account owners for customer notifications and follow-ups

Definitions and conventions:
- Cutover window: the scheduled maintenance window for the migration/swap.
- Chronicle entry: a timestamped operator log item (see "Evidence bundle" section).
- Safemode: a preconfigured degraded mode that preserves request-level SLA while isolating migration traffic.
- Evidence bundle: archived set of logs, snapshots, and signed manifests required for regulated customers.

Prerequisites (must be green before starting):
1) Customer signoff on maintenance window and SLO impact (reference signed schedule in customer portal).
2) Preflight synthetic tests passing on canary environment (latency, 95th percentile, token-throughput).
3) KV cache snapshot and verification completed (hash checksums recorded).
4) Artifact provenance verified (image signatures checked against SBOMs).
5) Operator roster and escalation contacts published in the runbook header.

Quick reference SLOs to validate post-cutover:
- 95th percentile latency <= 250ms for generation endpoints (for the tenant workload profile).
- Error rate <= 0.5% (5xx and 429 combined) over a 10-minute sliding window.
- Token throughput within 10% of pre-cutover baseline during steady-state traffic simulation.

Operator chronicle (step-by-step procedure) — execute in order:
1. Preparation and preflight (T-90 to T-15 minutes)
   a. Announce operator readiness on #field-ops with timestamp and checklist hash.
   b. Snapshot control-plane state: `redwoodctl controlplane snapshot --name pre-cutover-{{timestamp}}` and record SHA256.
   c. Capture KV-cache hash: `redwoodctl kv snapshot --tenant {{tenant-id}} --out kv-{{timestamp}}.tar.gz` then `sha256sum`.
   d. Export current routing policy: `kubectl -n redwood get configmap routing-policy -o yaml > routing-{{timestamp}}.yaml`.
   e. Dump active connections count and GPU utilization: `kubectl -n runtime exec -it runtime-proxy -- ./metrics/dump-active.sh > metrics-{{timestamp}}.txt`
2. Canary switch (T0)
   a. Shift 1–5% of traffic to canary variant using weight-based routing.
   b. Wait 5 minutes; run preflight harness (synthetic QPS @ target latency).
   c. Collect canary metrics: latency p50/p95/p99, OOMs, threadpool stalls.
   d. If canary fails, immediately rollback weights to 100% baseline and run rollback checklist.
3. Progressive rollout (T+5 to T+N minutes)
   a. Increase weight in steps (5 -> 20 -> 50 -> 100) with pause windows.
   b. At each step: run smoke tests (100 synthetic requests across representative prompt families).
   c. Operator records a chronicle entry after each step with: operator, timestamp, step weight, smoke test result, artifact versions, checksum.
4. Finalization and evidence capture (post-100% migration)
   a. Repeat snapshots (control plane, KV, routing).
   b. Create evidence manifest (see Evidence bundle manifest template).
   c. Notify customer of successful cutover and provide evidence bundle link (S3 pre-signed or customer portal artifact).

Rollback decision matrix (simplified):
- Immediate rollback triggers:
  - Any sustained p95 latency regression > 2x baseline for > 5 minutes
  - Error rate > 2% for > 3 minutes
  - Memory OOMs detected on > 10% of serving workers
- Controlled rollback: gradually reduce weights and redirect to previous model variant; follow Rollback steps below.

Controlled rollback steps:
1) Pause rollout and declare rollback intent in operator chronicle and #field-ops.
2) Revert routing policy to saved pre-cutover artifact: `kubectl apply -f routing-{{pre-cutover-timestamp}}.yaml`.
3) Restore KV cache snapshot if KV divergence detected: `redwoodctl kv restore --tenant {{tenant}} --snapshot kv-{{pre-cutover-timestamp}}.tar.gz` and validate checksums.
4) Monitor SLOs and collect rollback evidence (logs, metrics, core dumps).
5) Open an incident stub in PagerDuty and attach the evidence bundle.

Evidence bundle (what to collect and how):
- Required files (naming convention preserved):
  - `chronicle-{{timestamp}}.log` — operator timeline with ISO8601 timestamps.
  - `controlplane-snapshot-{{timestamp}}.json` — control plane snapshot exported via `redwoodctl` (signed).
  - `kv-snapshot-{{timestamp}}.tar.gz` + `kv-snapshot-{{timestamp}}.sha256`
  - `routing-{{timestamp}}.yaml` (pre and post)
  - `metrics-{{timestamp}}.txt` (GPU/utilization/connection counts)
  - `smoke-results-{{timestamp}}.json` (harness output)
  - `evidence-manifest-{{timestamp}}.txt` (see template below, signed by operator PGP key)
- Packaging: tar.gz the set and upload to the customer artifact store with a signed manifest. Example: `tar czf evidence-{{timestamp}}.tgz chronicle-*.log controlplane-*.json kv-*.tar.gz routing-*.yaml metrics-*.txt smoke-results-*.json evidence-manifest-*.txt`

Evidence manifest template (copy into `evidence-manifest-{{timestamp}}.txt`):
- operator: {{operator_name}}
- operator_email: {{operator_email}}
- tenant: {{tenant_id}}
- cutover_window: {{start}} to {{end}} (UTC)
- artifacts: [controlplane-snapshot-{{ts}}.json, kv-snapshot-{{ts}}.tar.gz, routing-{{ts}}.yaml, smoke-results-{{ts}}.json]
- sha256s: (list each with hex)
- signature: (PGP signature block)

Customer communication templates (preflight, in-flight, and post-cutover)
- Preflight (72–24 hours before window) — email subject and body
Subject: Planned maintenance: Redwood inference cutover for {{tenant_name}} on {{date}}
Body:
Hello {{customer_contact}},

This message confirms the planned maintenance window scheduled for {{date}} from {{start}} to {{end}} UTC. During the window we will perform an orchestrated cutover that may cause brief, controlled latency increases. Expected impact: up to 2 minutes of transient latency at each rollout step and a temporary reduction to 95% throughput for the first 10 minutes after finalization.

What we will do:
- Canary validation, progressive weight-based rollout, finalization and evidence delivery.

If you require stricter guardrails (no consumer-facing error budget impact), reply to this email and we will migrate using staggered tenant shadowing outside the listed window.

Best regards,
Maya Chen
Redwood Inference — Field Ops

- In-flight (short Slack/Email for major events)
Slack message (channel: #cust-{{customer}}-ops):
`[T+5m] Canary validated -> increasing to 20%`
`[T+25m] Reached 50% weight; smoke tests passed`
`[T+40m] Finalizing; collecting evidence bundle`

- Post-cutover (email with evidence link)
Subject: Cutover completed: Evidence and validation for {{tenant_name}} on {{date}}
Body:
Hello {{customer_contact}},

Cutover completed successfully at {{completion_ts}} UTC. Attached is the evidence bundle and manifest. Summary:
- Finalized model variant: {{model-name}} (sha256: {{model-sha}})
- Key validation metrics: p95 latency {{p95}} ms, error rate {{err_rate}}% 
- Snapshots and logs are available for download at: {{signed_url}} (expires in 30 days)

If you need longer retention or a deeper forensic package for audit, contact your Redwood account manager and we will open a support ticket.

Regards,
Maya Chen

Post-cutover validation checklist (10-minute, 1-hour, 24-hour cadence)
- 10-minute: confirm no new 5xx spikes, p95 within threshold, consumer-facing latencies stable
- 1-hour: run sample workload at 50% production QPS for 15 minutes and compare token throughput to baseline
- 24-hour: validate billing/quotas, telemetry ingestion consistency, and long-tail regression via the eval harness

Escalation & ownership
- Primary: Operator on call (listed in header)
- Secondary: Runtime SRE (pager on-call)
- Tertiary: Head of Field Engineering (for regulatory escalations)

Retention and evidence delivery policy
- Default artifact retention: 30 days in the customer portal
- For regulated customers, evidence may be delivered as a signed bundle with 1-year retention on request (requires contract amendment and support ticket).

Appendix A — sample CLI snippets and example smoke test JSON
- redwoodctl controlplane snapshot --name pre-cutover-20260115T0900Z --output controlplane-pre.json
- redwoodctl kv snapshot --tenant tenant-abc --out kv-20260115T0900Z.tar.gz
- Example smoke-results-20260115.json:
{
  "tenant": "tenant-abc",
  "run_ts": "2026-01-15T09:10:00Z",
  "tests": [{"id": "short-completion", "p95": 120, "ok": true}, {"id": "long-context", "p95": 210, "ok": true}]
}

Appendix B — quick timeline table (text)
| phase | operator action | expected duration | artifact created |
| Preflight | snapshots, signatures | 15–60m | controlplane-*, kv-* |
| Canary | 1–5% traffic | 5–15m | smoke-results-canary |
| Progressive | stepwise weights | 30–90m | chronicle-entries |
| Finalize | snapshots & manifest | 10–20m | evidence bundle |
